payloadShape.value: { name, unit, dims, note, archivedAt, createdAt }

unitIsTheRateSymbol.value: unit is what the account is measured in and is also its rate symbol: either a row of the operator's table or free text for a holding with no market price. There is no separate rate-symbol field, because two fields could disagree and a gram-versus-troy-ounce mismatch is silent

unitNamesTheBaseAssetOnly.value: the quote currency is the user's main currency and travels as a separate quote parameter, so a pair like USDCHF is never a unit

formattingPrecisionSource.value: from the symbol table's kind, currency or metal, and from a sensible default for free text. An explicit kind on the account would be a third copy of the same fact

dimsShape.value: a map from dimension id to value id, both opaque ids from the profile's dimension config, carrying no display text. A JSON object cannot carry the same key twice, so a second value for one dimension is unrepresentable

dimensionIdFormat.value: 8 characters of [a-z0-9], generated client-side at creation. Never a label-derived key, which could collide with a string already in user data

missingDimsEntry.value: a real state, rendered as Unassigned, never an error and never hidden. Nothing is backfilled at dimension-creation time. A value id naming no configured value, because the value or its dimension was archived, also renders as Unassigned, and the entry stays on the account untouched

noServerSideDimensionEntity.value: a server-side list would leak the classification graph. Everything the UI shows is derived client-side from the decrypted profile and accounts

archivedAt.value: null for an active account, otherwise the ISO date the account was archived

deleteIsAUserChoice.value: an account with snapshots presents two explicit options, archive preselected as the default, and permanent delete. An account with no snapshots skips the dialog and is deleted outright

archiveFlow.value: sets archivedAt and re-writes the account record. The account disappears from active lists and takes no new snapshots, every snapshot stays, and it is reversible. The dialog offers a closing snapshot dated archivedAt, prefilled with 0 and editable, and it is a recording action like any other, so it refreshes prices at archivedAt including the unit of the account being archived. The user may skip it, and either way the date carries an archive annotation

archiveOntoAnOccupiedDate.value: the closing-snapshot field prefills with the existing value rather than 0 and saving replaces that record in place. No replace prompt fires, because the field is showing the stored figure, and the dialog's own confirm is the confirmation

purge.value: DELETE /api/accounts/<account_id>?mode=purge removes the account record and cascades to every snapshot carrying that account_id, server-side and atomically. It deletes no price entry, because a price belongs to a symbol and the symbol is inside the ciphertext. Requires typing the account name to confirm, and the dialog states plainly that past net-worth figures will change

cascadeReach.value: no other record type carries an account link, so nothing else can be swept up by the cascade

namesAreNotUnique.value: two accounts may share a name. The record_id is identity

unitIsFrozenOnceRecorded.value: changing the unit of an account that already has snapshots is blocked, because the existing quantities are counted in the old unit and a new unit would price the whole history off a different symbol's series. Client-enforced by construction, since unit lives inside the ciphertext. Renaming, re-classifying and editing the note are always allowed

everyWriteReEncrypts.value: every write re-encrypts the whole record with a fresh nonce and increments version

renderingRule.value: decrypted names, notes and dimension labels are rendered with x-text or textContent only, never x-html

staleVersionOnEdit.condition: a concurrent edit from a second tab. The UI reloads and asks the user to redo the edit (spec/features/manage-accounts.md#edge-cases)

purgeOnAnotherUsersAccount.condition: Not Found, never Forbidden, and nothing is deleted (spec/features/manage-accounts.md#acceptance-criteria)

fixtures: an account with snapshots and an account without, for the two delete paths
an account whose archive date already holds a snapshot, for the prefill-and-no-prompt assertion
a second seeded vault owner holding an account, for the purge isolation assertion
a fault injected mid-purge, for the atomicity assertion
a profile holding an archived dimension and an archived value, plus accounts carrying entries that name them
an account name, a note and a dimension label each containing an XSS payload, for the literal-text assertion in the list, the chart legend and every tooltip
an account whose unit is free text and one whose unit is a listed symbol, for the rate-request-count assertion
focus: the unit-change block must be asserted against the UI refusing it, not against an API call being rejected. The server cannot see the unit, so a test written against the endpoint asserts a control that does not exist and would pass against a client that allows the change
purge must be shown to delete no rate record, asserted by count before and after, because the failure is silent and only shows up later as a repriced history
purge atomicity needs a fault injected mid-delete, with neither the account record nor its snapshots partially gone afterwards

archiving onto an occupied date must show no replace prompt and must leave exactly one snapshot for that (account, date) at version + 1. Half of this rule is about something not appearing, which no happy-path test catches

'no account record contains a rate symbol distinct from its unit' is asserted against the record shape itself, so that the 31x mismatch has nowhere to live. A value-level check would pass a schema that still admits the field
renaming a dimension label must leave every account record byte-identical, compared row by row rather than by counting writes
an account whose dims names an archived value must render as Unassigned with no account record written in either direction, restore included
the XSS assertion has to cover every place a decrypted string reaches, the list, the chart legend and every tooltip, not just the account form, because the rendering path differs between them
